title: Class 1 integron-associated resistance genes link hospital and household wastewater to an urban river in Bangladesh and persist through on-site effluent treatment
description: Hospital and household wastewater carry antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) into rivers, but in many low- and middle-income settings this flow is uncharacterised and on-site effluent treatment is rarely evaluated. We used shotgun metagenomics to follow the acquired resistome and mobilome from two hospitals, a residential area and the receiving Bhairab River in Jashore, Bangladesh. Nine composite sludge and sediment samples were collected along the continuum: inlet and discharge points of a hospital without an effluent treatment plant (ETP), the release and discharge points of a hospital with an ETP, two household drainage points, and river sites upstream and downstream of the outfalls and at a distant control. Reads were annotated against MEGARes v3.0 and a mobile genetic element (MGE) database; chromosomal entries that require SNP confirmation were excluded and used as a housekeeping (HK) normaliser. In total, 162,263 hits to 403 acquired ARG gene groups and 497,626 MGE hits were obtained. Acquired ARG abundance fell 30-fold from the untreated hospital inlet (1,074 per 1,000 HK hits) to the river control (36), and carbapenemase (blaKPC, blaNDM, blaVIM, blaIMP) and last-resort resistance genes (mcr, tet(X), optrA, cfr, vanA) were essentially confined to the untreated hospital. ARG abundance tracked the class 1 integron integrase gene intI1 (Spearman rho = 0.88, P = 0.002) and IS6-family (IS26-like) elements (rho = 0.97, P < 0.001), and genes typically carried as integron cassettes correlated more strongly with intI1 than other ARGs (median rho 0.93 vs 0.66, P = 0.014). Quaternary ammonium compound (qac) and mercury (mer) resistance genes followed intI1 closely (rho 0.88-0.95). The hospital with an ETP released three-fold fewer ARGs than the hospital without one, but integron-borne genes were disproportionately retained: 81% of cassette ARGs detected at the untreated hospital were also found after treatment, compared with 38% of other ARGs. Downstream river sediment was more similar than upstream sediment to every source sample, and all of its ARG gene groups also occurred in the sources. Class 1 integrons and IS26 thus link the hospital resistome to the river and resist current effluent treatment, which supports intI1-based monitoring of hospital outfalls and treatment that targets the integron-borne fraction of the resistome.
